recent_items.summary: World models are increasingly judged by how well they rank plausible futures, yet plausibility alone is the wrong target. recent_items.summary: The goal of a world model is to capture the dynamics of an environment. This has the great appeal that it allows agents to plan and simulate a course of actions with the help of a world model. For these uses to be reliable, however, the learned dynamics must behave well beyond the specific state-action combinations observed in expert rollouts. recent_items.title: AnyGoal: On World Model Generalization Beyond Expert Rollouts

Models often silently alter given quantities, fabricate laws, or inject unstated assumptions to force a problem into familiar patterns, and then reason inside this corrupted world. recent_items.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are trained through multi-stage pipelines over heterogeneous data sources, yet developers lack a principled way to pinpoint the specific data responsible for an observed behavior. recent_items.title: DebugLM: Learning Traceable Training Data Provenance for LLMs

recent_items.title: Simulation Priors for Rapid Adaptation in Model-Based RL for Autonomous Racing

recent_items.summary: Model--harness co-evolution has emerged as a prominent paradigm for recursive self-improving (RSI) agents, jointly evolving their execution scaffolds and intrinsic capabilities. We study the persistent yet often overlooked brain--body mismatch problem in this paradigm, where an evolving harness (body) demands behaviors its model (brain) has not learned or restricts capabilities it already possesses. recent_items.title: CoEvo-RSI: When Harnesses Evolve, Which Models Should Follow?

recent_items.title: LeakBench: Auditing Reward Hacking through Prediction-Time Leakage in Clinical Modeling Agents
